pairs.subject: bounded-enumeration
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/load.ts:116 Runs reads kernel jobs through `list(store)`, which has no limit and no seek: it pulls every row of the jobs table into memory and parses it, then keeps only the last KERNEL_CAP. So the cost of this read grows with the table, not with the cap (the file's own header admits "list() itself has no limit yet").

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/load.ts:121 The bound is an in-memory slice after a full SELECT ordered by ord, n. There is no position-plus-limit seek. The ledger read on line 95 does pass a limit to queryEvents correctly.

app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/load.ts:43 KERNEL_CAP = 500 and LEDGER_CAP = 1000 are round numbers. No memory target or worst-case row size is recorded beside them, and they cannot be overridden at deploy time.
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/load.ts:120 The clamp is not silent. Truncation shows up as a `problem` the page renders, and the ledger page's `capped` flag does the same on line 100.
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/load.ts:95 Each render reads one page and never follows the continuation, so there is no multi-page walk whose consistency would need stating.
